This Wp Is Filed Under Articles 226 And 227 Of
The Constitution Of India Praying To Quash The Fir

Police Station Against The Petitioner U/S 498A, 323,
504, 506 Of Ipc By Allowing The Above Petition.
 This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
Order Was Made Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice M.Nagaprasanna
 Oral Order

The petitioner - husband is before this Court calling in question registration of a crime in Crime
No.179/2023 pending before the 30th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nrupatunga Road,
Bengaluru City, for the offences under Sections 498A, 504, 323 and 506 of the Ipc.

2. Heard Sri Shreyas B.S., learned counsel for petitioner, Smt. Sowmya R., learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and Sri Keshav M. Datar, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
NC: 2024:KHC:32068 3.

A co-ordinate bench of this Court, owing to the submissions of the learned counsel for petitioner,
had granted an interim order of stay on 11.03.2024, which reads as follows:
"Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that on the basis of a similar complaint made by respondent no.2/Complainant, FIR in Crime No.42/2023 is registered by Kempapura Agrahara Police and for the very same offences, on the basis of a second complaint yet again a case is registered in Crime No.179/2023 by the very same K V Hari Vittal vs State Of Karnataka on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132034332/
2 Police.

sentences.text:
Learned HCGP is directed to take notice for respondent no.1.
Issue emergent notice to respondent no.2.
There shall be an interim order as prayed for as against the petitioner, till the next date of hearing."

The afore-quoted interim order was granted on the score that there are two crimes registered, one in Crime No.42/2023 and another in Crime No.179/2023, on the very same cause of action and for the very same offences.

4. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has filed an application - I.A.No.1/2024 seeking vacation of the interim NC: 2024:KHC:32068 order, which clearly demonstrates that the first offence emerges for an act of assault by the petitioner on 06.04.2023.
Therefore, it becomes a crime in Crime No.42/2023 for it having been registered, on 07.04.2023.
The second crime emerges on a further assault by the husband on 14.10.2023, which then becomes the impugned Crime No.179/2023.
Therefore, the two crimes cannot be hit by doctrine of sameness, as they arise on two different incidents at two different times, at a gap of 6 months.
The parties may be the same, the assault may be the same, but the cause of action is entirely different.
The common stream that runs through both these crimes is Section 498A of the IPC.

There is no such allegation in the complaint against the petitioner that would touch upon the ingredients of Section 498A of the IPC, as in the second crime in Crime No.42/2023 investigation is pending.
5. In that light, except Section 498A of the IPC, all other offences are required to be investigated as it is not hit by doctrine of sameness, except Section 498A of the IPC.
There cannot be any repeated cases of Section 498A of the IPC, being registered on the very same cause of action of demand of NC: 2024:KHC:32068 dowry.

Therefore, the offence under Section 498A of the IPC as registered in crime No.179/2023 stands obliterated and all other offences so registered stand sustained.
6.

For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The writ petition is allowed in-part.

(ii) The offence under Section 498A of the IPC registered in Crime No.179/2023,
pending before the 30th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, stands quashed and the investigation shall continue qua the other offences.
(iii) It is made clear that the findings or the observations made in the course of the order does not relate to Crime No.42/2023, at all.
